newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.
newsitem.headline: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.

text.p: Vacant primary elevator space tightened in the past week across Canada's Prairies as railcar unloads at Pacific ports fell below targets for another week since early January, a Canadian Wheat Board spokeswoman said.
Average vacancy in Prairie elevators was 18 percent in the week ended Feb 16 compared to 21 percent the week before, CWB spokeswoman Tracey Thompson said.

The CWB said it faces C$15 million in demurrage fines because of grain shipment delays to export position from the Prairies since early January. Forty-one vessels waited to load on the Pacific coast Friday. One ship waited up to 43 days.
Primary elevator vacancy in Manitoba was the tightest at 16 percent, followed by Saskatchewan at 18 percent and Alberta at 19 percent, Thompson said.
Railcar unloads at Vancouver totalled 2,484, or 82.8 percent of the 3,000 hopper car target for the week, she said.
Railcar unloads at Prince Rupert reached 1,157, or 89 percent of the 1,300 hopper car target for the week, she said.
Railcar unloads at Thunder Bay totalled 485, or 98.9 percent of the 490 hopper car target for the week, she said.
